transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-14
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya, Lucas, Rita (Sycamore)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Morgan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Priya and I will run through the Console — primarily route-level telemetry, cost breakdowns, and how you can map those to chargeback. Uh, feel free to interrupt, ask questions.
[00:12] Maya: Hi Alex, hi Priya. Thanks — we've been looking forward to this. We mainly want to see how per-route costs show up, and how we'd use that for FinOps.
[00:20] Priya: Great. Quick agenda: 1) overview of usage analytics in the Console; 2) per-route dashboards and filters; 3) cost decomposition (token level, model variant, infra); 4) telemetry exports and integration with your billing system.
[00:36] Lucas: Quick note — our stack is an internal API gateway -> service mesh -> Redwood hosted endpoints for inference. We're on GCP and also evaluating dedicated capacity for steady-state workloads.
[00:47] Rita: And from FinOps, our ask is to be able to attribute costs to product teams by route, and to spot spikes fast.
[00:54] Priya: Perfect. Opening the Console now — sorry if the colors look off, my screen share is a little laggy. Ok, top-left you see the global usage lens. This is aggregate RPS, tokens, cost burn over time.
[01:10] [01:12] Alex: One thing to highlight — token-level unit economics are visible per-route and per-model. You can group by model family, and we show an estimate of inferred GPU time which helps separate model cost vs infra cost.
[01:22] Maya: That GPU time estimate — is that measured or modeled?
[01:25] Priya: It's modeled from our runtime telemetry plus kernel selection heuristics. For dedicated clusters we have tighter measurements; for hosted we infer from request shape and observed latencies. Occasionally the name gets scrambled in the export — our logs might say "K V cache" separately.
[01:38] Lucas: Can we tag routes to product lines? We want to map route => product => team.
[01:42] Priya: Absolutely. Routes support tag metadata; tags propagate through the route-level dashboard and also populate the CSV export for billing.
[01:50] Rita: Show an example of a cost spike root cause?
[01:53] Priya: Sure — clicking into the "Payments-API / invoice-generation" route. This view shows token breakdown (prompt vs completion), model used (gpt-like-3-small in this example), average latency P95, and a stacked cost graph where you can toggle caching savings and batching effect.
[02:10] [02:15] Alex: You'll notice a sharp increase at 10:32 last Thursday — that was due to a change in prompt size and a fallback to a larger model when the smaller model hit an error. The Console surfaces that via our anomaly detector and shows the policy fallback path.
[02:28] Maya: The anomaly alerts — can they integrate with our PagerDuty?
[02:31] Priya: Yes, alerts can route to webhook, PagerDuty, or Slack. You can set thresholds on token burn, latency SLOs, or sudden model switch frequency.
[02:38] Lucas: For dedicated vs hosted decision — what guidance do you give in the Console about cost vs latency?
[02:44] Priya: We have an Optimize panel that simulates cost at different quantization and route batching settings. For example, for high-throughput routes, dedicated with 8-bit quantization plus continuous batching lowered unit cost by ~35% in a similar customer workload. Those are simulations, and we recommend running a small pilot to validate.
[03:00] [03:05] Rita: Is the quantization recommendation per-model? We have custom fine-tuned variants.
[03:09] Priya: Yes, recommendations are per model and per route. We factor in your sequence length distribution and model architecture. For fine-tuned models we run a short eval to estimate quality impact before suggesting quantization levels.
[03:19] Maya: On security — we need SOC 2 and SSO. Also KMS for encryption at rest. What do we need to see in the Console for auditability?
[03:28] Alex: Great question. The Console includes an audit log export with token-level call traces (scrubbed for PII by default), model version pinning history, rollout events (canary AB), and SSO sign-in events. For Private deployment we support customer KMS/HSM integrations.
[03:41] Lucas: How's the RBAC set up? We want separation between product engineers and FinOps.
[03:45] Priya: Role-based access with customizable roles — you can create a "FinOps Viewer" role scoped to billing and route dashboards only. We also support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning.
[03:54] Rita: Okay good. Show CSV export for chargeback.
[03:57] [04:00] Priya: Exporting now — the CSV has columns: route, tags, model_version, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, estimated_gpu_ms, cost_model, cost_inference, cost_infra, date. You can ingest this into your billing pipeline; we've seen customers link the routes column to internal chargeback keys.
[04:18] Maya: Any pitfalls — we've seen mismatch between token-metering and our billing because of client-side retries.
[04:24] Alex: We recommend instrumenting idempotency keys and using our request id header. The Console tries to de-dupe obvious double-sends, but client-side retry noise will inflate usage if not deduped upstream.
[04:36] Lucas: Regarding caching — we heard about prefix caching and KV cache. How does that show up?
[04:41] Priya: Prefix caching is surfaced as a cache hit-rate per route and estimated token-savings. KV cache shows up for streaming sessions — we display average KV cache hit ratio per model variant. Note: sometimes the transcription in our export labels that as "K B cache" — apologies for the audio, catalog quirks.
[04:59] [05:05] Alex: Walkthrough of a sample dashboard — starting from top you can apply filters (date range, team tag, model family). Then the route list sorts by cost impact; you can pin important routes to a watchlist and subscribe to weekly reports.
[05:17] Rita: Can we create a report that splits cost by team monthly and pushes to SFTP?
[05:20] Priya: Yes — scheduled reports can be emailed, pushed to S3/GCS, or delivered to an SFTP endpoint. We also support scheduled exports in parquet for large datasets.
[05:30] Maya: On the model fallback you mentioned — how do automatic fallback policies affect cost visibility? If a fallback to cheaper model happens, is that visible?
[05:39] Priya: We record policy decisions in the request trace. The route trace shows original model requested, fallback model chosen, and associated costs per attempt. That is visible in the per-request CSV and the aggregated dashboard.
[05:52] [06:00] Alex: Let's demo a shorter timeline: here we narrow to last 24 hours for the "chat-assist" route. You can see per-minute token burn. Because you have spikes at business hours, you might want to apply a burst policy or route some traffic to a cheaper model during non-critical interactions.
[06:15] Lucas: For a pilot we'll likely pick 3 routes: chat-assist, invoice-generation, and search-rerank. Can we get per-route SLOs?
[06:23] Priya: Yes — you can define latency and availability SLOs per route and have the Console surface SLO breaches and their cost impact.
[06:30] Rita: If we do reserved capacity, can you show modeled ROI in the Console?
[06:33] Priya: There's an ROI modeler — plug in your expected qps and token shapes and the Console compares hosted pay-as-you-go vs Reserved / Dedicated commitments including burst costs. It's a simulation but we've found it to be within 5-10% vs actual for customers with similar footprints.
[06:49] [07:00] Maya: Any examples of customers in finance/healthcare? We have regulatory needs and curious about Private deployment.
[07:05] Alex: We have several. For regulated workloads we recommend Private (VPC) with customer KMS, HSM optional, and private control plane. The Console still looks identical, but the control plane endpoints are in your VPC.
[07:17] Lucas: How do we get logs out for SIEM?
[07:20] Priya: You can stream audit logs to your SIEM (S3/GCS/Splunk/Elastic). We support structured JSON events and a high-throughput log forwarder.
[07:31] Rita: Pricing asks — how granular is invoicing? By route? By model? Do we get monthly line items?
[07:37] Alex: Invoice line items are configurable; many customers prefer per-route chargeback and summary per-model family. We can provide monthly CSVs with whichever granularity you want.
[07:46] Maya: We also want to experiment with model variants — one of our concerns is quality regressions when you change quantization levels.
[07:53] Priya: That's why we include eval hooks in Optimize: run your prompt set against a candidate quantized model and compare outputs to a baseline. We also track quality drift over time tied to your sample prompts.
[08:07] [08:15] Alex: There was a question in the pre-meeting notes about demoing the route-level anomaly timeline. Priya — can you show the annotated runbook?
[08:20] Priya: Sure — clicking into anomaly timeline: we annotate events (deploy, scale, policy change, fallback). Each annotation links to the exact request trace. You can attach runbook steps and a post-mortem template directly in the Console.
[08:33] Lucas: That would be helpful. Does runbook editing support approvals and signoffs?
[08:36] Priya: We have a comments/approval workflow integrated with SSO identities — it's lightweight, not a full ITSM, but good for quick signoffs.
[08:46] Rita: Okay, show the billing forecast feature.
[08:49] [08:52] Priya: Forecasting uses historical daily burn and then simulates seasonalities and expected growth. In this example you can add a planned product launch event which spikes token demand by 2x for three days and the forecast updates instantly.
[09:04] Maya: If the forecast exceeds our reserved capacity, will the Console suggest autoscale or burst settings?
[09:09] Priya: Yes — it will recommend burst policies and estimated burst costs. It can also suggest moving some non-critical routes to a cheaper model variant for the launch window.
[09:20] Lucas: We need to validate token accounting against our own metering. Will you run a reconciliation?
[09:26] Alex: We typically run a reconciliation during pilot. Priya will share the scripts and mapping table.
[09:31] Priya: I'll share a reconciliation workbook (CSV mapping table) — we can run it together during the pilot and adjust dedupe rules.
[09:37] [09:40] Rita: On SSO provisioning — our security team asked about SAML attributes for team membership.
[09:45] Priya: We accept standard attributes, and groups map to Console roles. We can also support SCIM for user provisioning.
[09:50] Maya: What about retention for logs?
[09:53] Alex: Default retention is 90 days in the hosted plan; enterprise/Private can extend retention or route logs to your long-term storage.
[09:59] Lucas: Are there any limitations on export frequency? We want near real-time exports for chargeback.
[10:04] Priya: Exports can be scheduled as frequently as hourly. For near real-time needs we recommend the event stream integration which pushes per-request events to your collector.
[10:12] [10:20] Alex: Let's walk through the pilot proposal: 30-day pilot, instrument three routes, compare hosted vs dedicated simulation, run cache/batching benchmarks, do a short quality eval on quantized variants, and reconcile usage.
[10:32] Maya: Sounds good. Timeline wise, can we start the pilot by end of month?
[10:36] Alex: If we get sign-off this week we can spin up instrumentation and have benchmarks in 7–10 days.
[10:44] Rita: Anything else we need from our side?
[10:47] Priya: Sample payloads for the three routes, expected qps and SLOs, and a short prompt set for the eval.
[10:54] Maya: We'll send those.
[10:57] [11:00] Lucas: A quick technical follow-up — can you share the endpoint headers and recommended middleware for idempotency and request tracing?
[11:06] Priya: Yes — I'll include the header spec in the follow-up packet: x-rw-request-id, x-rw-model-hint, x-rw-client-retry.
[11:15] Alex: We're also going to include security docs link and SOC 2 report once we have NDA signed if needed.
[11:20] Maya: NDA is in flight.
[11:22] Priya: One note about cost delta visualizations — for long tails of low-volume routes, the Console suggests batch windows; for real-time chats we recommend continuous batching with small windows to reduce overhead without harming latency.
[11:36] [11:40] Alex: Ok I want to call out a common objection — "we can't move to Dedicated because of burst traffic" — we handle that with hybrid routing: steady-state to Dedicated, burst to Hosted, with automated fallbacks. The Console shows the routing split and estimated savings.
[11:58] Rita: Neat. How are model rollouts handled in the Console? We need safe rollouts.
[12:04] Priya: Canary and phased rollouts are supported with automatic rollback on degradation. You can tie rollouts to eval metrics so if quality drops we revert and notify your team.
[12:16] Maya: That should help.
[12:18] [12:22] Alex: Alright, quick recap and next steps: Alex to send pricing + pilot statement, Priya to run benchmarks and share scripts, Sycamore to provide payloads and compliance contact. We'll schedule the pilot kickoff for next week tentatively.
[12:38] Rita: Thanks all.
[12:41] Maya: Thanks, that was very helpful.
[12:43] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invite.

End of transcript.
